faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Honest answers to the questions budget travelers actually ask.

cheaper.question: Why are you cheaper than other private Egypt tours?
cheaper.answer: Because we don't pad the price with things you didn't ask for. Most Egypt tour packages bundle hotels, meals, tickets, and concierge service into a single number — even if you'd rather choose those yourself. AffordEgypt charges only for the operational core: a private car, a licensed Egyptologist, and a transparent base price from {{floor}}/day. You add tickets, meals, and experiences only when you want them. Same operations as Capital Travel Service's premium tier, with the markup and the inclusions you didn't choose stripped out.

scam.question: How do I know AffordEgypt isn't one of the scam operators I've read about?
scam.answer: Fair question — there are real scam operators in Egypt, and we don't blame anyone for being cautious. AffordEgypt is operated by Capital Travel Service, which is registered with the Egyptian Travel Agents Association (ETAA 2179) and has been operating in Cairo since 2003 with thousands of documented travelers. Every guide we work with is a licensed Egyptologist with an active Ministry of Tourism credential. You can verify our registration with ETAA directly. We also publish our prices, our inclusions, and our cancellation terms before you pay anything.

licensed.question: Are your guides actually licensed Egyptologists?
licensed.answer: Yes — every guide we send is licensed by the Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities and carries a current Egyptologist credential. This isn't a small thing: unlicensed guides can't legally take you past the front gates of major sites, and many cheaper operators send them anyway. Our guides are the same roster Capital Travel Service uses for premium tours — they just deliver the lighter inclusions tier when working under AffordEgypt.

payment.question: How does payment work? Do I have to pay everything up front?
payment.answer: No — that's part of the point. You pay a 10% deposit when you book (we send you a payment link, usually via Tab.travel, that works with any major card). Your booking is confirmed once the deposit clears. The remaining 90% is paid on arrival in cash (we accept EGP, USD, EUR, or GBP), via a second payment link, or by card through our mobile reader. Whatever's easiest for you.

cancellation.question: What's your cancellation policy?
cancellation.answer: Free cancellation up to 48 hours before your trip starts — you get the full deposit back. Inside 48 hours, the deposit is non-refundable because we've already committed your guide and vehicle for those days. Anything paid beyond the deposit is refunded in full. If we have to cancel for any reason on our end (vehicle issue, guide illness, force majeure), we refund 100%, including the deposit, and help you rebook.

customize.question: Can I customize my itinerary?
customize.answer: Yes. Our entire model is modular — pick destinations, pick how many days in each, pick which attractions to include, add a guide for some days but not others, choose vehicle size by group. The pricing tool builds it live. If you want something the tool doesn't show, message us on WhatsApp and we'll quote it manually.

minimum.question: What's the absolute minimum I could pay for a private Egypt trip?
minimum.answer: Our floor is {{floor}}/day for a private car + licensed Egyptologist in Cairo, before tickets, meals, and hotel. A typical 3-day Cairo trip with all entrance tickets and one meal per day works out to around LE 14,000–18,000 per person for a couple, depending on which attractions you include. We'll send you a real quote in under a minute — no account, no commitment. Note: we don't sell shared minibus tours. Some operators advertise "Egypt tours from $50/day" — those are shared group tours, a different product. Ours is fully private.

ticketFee.question: Why do you charge 50 EGP to arrange an entrance ticket?
ticketFee.answer: The attraction keeps its official admission price; the additional 50 EGP is AffordEgypt's optional advance-arrangement fee for each paid ticket issued. We purchase and organize the ticket before the visit, check the booking information supplied to us, and prepare it for the tour. This can reduce time at the ticket office and avoids relying entirely on on-site card payment, which matters because many Egyptian sites are now cashless and payment or ticketing systems can occasionally experience technical problems. It does not bypass security or other entrance controls. You can see the official prices and buy directly on the Ministry's own ticket portal, and the move to e-ticketing is described in the State Information Service announcement.

buyTickets.question: Can I buy the entrance tickets myself?
buyTickets.answer: Yes. The service is optional. You may buy tickets through the attraction's official booking channel or an approved on-site sales point where available. If you ask us to arrange them, your quote will show the official admission amount and our 50 EGP fee separately — we never fold the two together and call it the entrance fee.

feePerTicket.question: Is the 50 EGP ticket fee charged once per booking?
feePerTicket.answer: No. It is charged per paid admission ticket issued. Two visitors ordering admission to four attractions require eight tickets, so the service fee is 8 x 50 EGP = 400 EGP. Student or reduced-price tickets need valid supporting identification accepted by the attraction; without it the venue may require a full-price ticket.

skipQueue.question: Does an advance ticket mean we skip every queue?
skipQueue.answer: No. It can reduce or avoid the ticket-purchase queue. Security screening, ticket validation, identification checks, timed-entry controls, capacity restrictions, and other venue queues may still apply. Ticket changes, cancellations and refunds also remain subject to the attraction's own rules, which we state before collecting payment.

visa.question: Do I need a visa to enter Egypt?
visa.answer: Most travelers (US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, and most other passports) need a visa to enter Egypt. The easiest option is the Egypt e-Visa at visa2egypt.gov.eg — apply online a week before travel, costs $25 USD for single entry, and the approval comes by email. You can also get a visa on arrival at most major airports (Cairo, Hurghada, Sharm El Sheikh) for the same fee in cash USD or EUR. A few nationalities (most African, some Asian) have different rules — check Egypt's MOFA website or just message us on WhatsApp and we'll point you to the right info.

bestTime.question: When is the best time to visit Egypt?
bestTime.answer: October through April is the peak season — temperatures are pleasant (15–25°C / 60–77°F) across the whole country, including Upper Egypt (Luxor, Aswan, Abu Simbel). May through September gets very hot in Upper Egypt and the desert (40°C+ / 104°F+ is normal), though Cairo and the Mediterranean coast are still manageable. If you can travel in shoulder season (October–early November or late February–April), you get good weather with smaller crowds and better prices. We avoid sending travelers to Upper Egypt in July–August unless they specifically want the heat.

cairo.airportsTitle: First: Which Cairo Airport Are You Using?
cairo.airportsIntro: Cairo has two major passenger airports, and they are on opposite sides of Greater Cairo. Please check the three-letter airport code on your ticket before requesting a transfer.

airports.name: Cairo International Airport
airports.location: Located on the eastern side of Cairo, near Heliopolis.
airports.direct: Usually the more direct arrival airport for Heliopolis, Nasr City, Downtown Cairo, Zamalek, Maadi, and many New Cairo addresses.
airports.farther: Transfers to Giza, the Pyramids area, Sheikh Zayed City, and 6th of October City cross more of Greater Cairo, so the route and fare may be higher.

airports.name: Sphinx International Airport
airports.location: Located west of Cairo in Giza Governorate, near the Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road.
airports.direct: Usually the more direct arrival airport for Sheikh Zayed City, 6th of October City, the Grand Egyptian Museum, and many western Giza hotels.
airports.farther: Transfers to Downtown Cairo, Heliopolis, Nasr City, Maadi, or New Cairo travel farther across the metropolitan area and are quoted accordingly.

cairo.airportWarning: CAI and SPX are different airports. Selecting the wrong airport can change the route substantially. Send us your flight number so we can verify the arrival airport and monitor the correct flight.

luxor.banksTitle: First: Is Your Hotel on the East Bank or West Bank?
luxor.banksIntro: For many years, "Luxor airport transfer" usually meant a transfer to one of the established East Bank hotels. Luxor now has a much wider choice of hotels and guesthouses on the West Bank, so the hotel name and riverbank must be confirmed before an accurate fare can be given.
luxor.airportLocation: Luxor Airport is east of the city and on the eastern side of the Nile.
luxor.airportRouting: That makes many East Bank hotels comparatively direct by road. A West Bank hotel requires a different and generally longer driving route.

banks.name: East Bank Hotels
areas: Hotels around Khaled Ibn El Walid Street
Many large resort and international-brand hotels
banks.note: East Bank journeys do not require the vehicle to cross the Nile. The exact distance still varies because Luxor's East Bank hotel area extends north and south of the city centre.

banks.name: West Bank Hotels
areas: Hotels near the West Bank archaeological sites
Hager Al Dabayah and properties farther south
banks.note: For a normal private airport transfer, the vehicle travels by road across the Luxor bridge. The central passenger ferry is useful for people moving between the banks, but it is not the standard route for an airport vehicle carrying passengers and luggage. Because the road bridge is outside the central hotel area, a West Bank transfer is not the same journey as an East Bank transfer.

luxor.bankWarning: "West Bank" is not one single destination. A guesthouse near the ferry, a hotel near Medinet Habu, and a property farther south can require different routes. Send the property name, full address, or a map pin rather than only writing "Luxor West Bank."

aswan.heroNote: Your Aswan transfer fare depends on the exact destination — not only the word "Aswan." Send us the hotel, village, jetty, or cruise details and we will confirm the route and price before you book.
aswan.whereTitle: First: Where in Aswan Are You Staying?
aswan.whereIntro: An airport transfer to a central Corniche hotel is not the same journey as a transfer to an outlying resort, Gharb Soheil, an island-hotel launch point, or a cruise vessel docked outside the city centre. The exact destination determines the route, vehicle time, and final price.
aswan.airportLocation: Aswan International Airport is outside the city, south of central Aswan. Different accommodations can lie in different directions from the airport, so distance should be checked from the actual property rather than estimated from "Aswan city."

destinations.name: Central Aswan Hotels
areas: Hotels around the Nubian Museum and Old Cataract area
Central riverside properties with direct road access
destinations.note: Eligible central routes may receive the displayed starting price after the exact property is confirmed.

destinations.name: Hotels Outside Central Aswan
destinations.note: Some resorts, guesthouses, and accommodation use an Aswan address but are outside the central hotel area. A property near the High Dam road, in a southern district, north of the city, or in another outlying location may require a different fare. Send the full hotel name and a map pin. Similar property names and broad location labels can otherwise lead to the wrong route.

destinations.name: Gharb Soheil and Nubian Village Stays
destinations.note: Gharb Soheil — also written Gharb Suhail, Gharb Sohail, or West Suhail — is a Nubian village area south of central Aswan on the west side of the Nile. Its airport route is different from a central Corniche transfer. Properties are spread across the village area, and vehicle access can vary by street and hotel entrance. Please send the exact guesthouse or hotel and a map pin. Do not select "Aswan city hotel" if your booking is in Gharb Soheil or another Nubian village.

destinations.name: Island Hotels and Boat Connections
destinations.intro: Hotels on Elephantine Island, other islands, or river locations without direct road access require a transfer to the correct mainland jetty rather than to the hotel door by car. The hotel's own launch, a public ferry, or a separately arranged boat may complete the journey. Confirm with the property:
areas: Whether the boat is included in the hotel booking
Whether staff will meet you at the jetty
destinations.note: Our quote will state whether it covers only the road transfer or also includes a separately confirmed boat connection.

aswan.lakeTitle: Nile Cruise or Lake Nasser Cruise?
aswan.lakeBody: These are not necessarily served from the same docking area. Standard Nile cruises between Aswan and Luxor commonly use Nile moorings in or around Aswan. Lake Nasser cruises use a different embarkation area associated with the High Dam side of Aswan. Tell us the complete itinerary and vessel name so we do not send the vehicle to the wrong dock.

aboutPage.seoDescription: AffordEgypt is the transparent budget tier of Capital Travel Service, an ETAA-licensed Cairo operator since 2003, founded by a guide from Aswan.
aboutPage.heroSubtitle: More than just a travel company - we're passionate Egypt specialists making authentic travel accessible to everyone.
aboutPage.missionBody: Afford Egypt is more than just a travel company; we are a dedicated team of passionate Egypt travel specialists who believe that everyone should have the opportunity to experience the magic of Egypt, regardless of their budget. Since our inception in 2003, we've proudly assisted thousands of travelers in exploring Egypt's unparalleled wonders without breaking the bank.
aboutPage.value1Body: Budget travel shouldn't mean compromising on safety. Our vehicles are regularly inspected and maintained, and our accommodations adhere to rigorous safety protocols.
aboutPage.value2Body: Being young travelers ourselves, we understand the needs of backpackers, friends seeking thrills, and couples on their first overseas adventure.
aboutPage.value3Body: Our transparent pricing model ensures families can plan confidently, knowing exactly what costs will be upfront with no hidden surprises.
aboutPage.story1Body: Afford Egypt also recognizes the challenges faced by families eager to discover Egypt without straining their finances. Traveling with children or extended family members can quickly become costly, and it's our mission to alleviate these financial pressures. Our transparent pricing model ensures that families can confidently plan their adventures, knowing exactly what their costs will be upfront. This approach eliminates surprises, enabling families to focus fully on enjoying their Egyptian experience.
aboutPage.story2Body: Our commitment extends beyond simply offering budget-friendly tours; it also includes connecting travelers with authentic local experiences. Afford Egypt collaborates closely with knowledgeable local guides who bring history to life through insightful stories and personal narratives. These interactions foster a deeper understanding and appreciation of Egypt's vibrant culture and ancient traditions. Moreover, our reliance on reliable local transportation means our guests enjoy smoother, more immersive journeys.
aboutPage.story3Body: In a market crowded with travel options, Afford Egypt stands out by championing transparency, affordability, and inclusivity. We reject the idea that exploring the world should only be accessible to the wealthy. Our youthful perspective empowers us to challenge industry norms, continuously seeking innovative ways to deliver incredible experiences at accessible prices. Every package we offer, from short city breaks to comprehensive nationwide tours, reflects our core philosophy of making travel dreams achievable for everyone.
aboutPage.story4Body: Furthermore, our customer support is exceptional, personal, and direct. We maintain open lines of communication with our travelers, assisting them from the initial planning stages through to their safe return home. Unlike larger companies, we do not rely on automated chatbots or impersonal interactions. Instead, every question, request, and feedback is managed directly by our dedicated team members, who are committed to ensuring each trip exceeds expectations.
aboutPage.promiseBody1: As we continue to grow, our promise remains unwavering: to provide exceptional, memorable experiences that don't compromise on quality, safety, or authenticity—even at budget-friendly prices. Afford Egypt isn't just about traveling affordably; it's about traveling smartly, safely, and sustainably.
aboutPage.promiseBody2: Join us and become part of a growing community of satisfied travelers who have discovered that exploring Egypt can be enriching, exciting, and affordable. Let Afford Egypt guide you through the splendors of ancient civilizations, modern culture, and everything in between—all while respecting your budget constraints and prioritizing your safety and well-being.
aboutPage.ctaBody: Afford Egypt is here to ensure it's unforgettable and accessible for everyone.

travelTips.seoTitle: Egypt Travel Tips | What Locals Wish You Knew
travelTips.seoDescription: Egypt travel tips from a Cairo-based licensed operator: visas, tipping, safety, scams, transport and money, and what guidebooks usually get wrong.
travelTips.heroLead: Get insider tips on transport, food, accommodation, and attractions.
travelTips.whyTitle: Why Egypt in 2026 Is a Budget Traveler's Dream
travelTips.whyP1: So, why does Egypt top the list for affordable travel in 2026? Let's start with the exchange rate. If you're arriving with US dollars, euros, or pounds, your money can go a long way here. The Egyptian Pound has seen some ups and downs over the past few years, and while inflation remains a concern locally, it often works in your favour as a visitor. Hotels, meals, transport, and even museum tickets can feel surprisingly affordable—especially when compared to what you'd spend for a similar experience in Europe or North America.
travelTips.whyP2: Another bonus? Egypt is actively investing in its tourism scene. Beyond the timeless pyramids and temple ruins, you'll now find cutting-edge museums, interactive exhibitions, and even digital experiences that blend ancient history with modern storytelling. And since many of these are newly launched, they often come with introductory pricing—a win for travelers who want more for less.
travelTips.bestTimesTitle: Best Times to Visit on a Budget
travelTips.bestTimesLead: When it comes to visiting Egypt, timing really is everything—especially if you're trying to stretch your budget without compromising comfort or adventure. Choosing the right season can make all the difference.
travelTips.checklistLead: Getting your travel documents sorted in advance is one of the smartest (and easiest!) ways to keep your Egyptian adventure stress-free.
travelTips.visaBody: Ensure your passport is valid for at least six months past your arrival. Most travelers need a visa. The
travelTips.visaBody2: is highly recommended and can be applied for online. Visa on Arrival is an option for some, but check rules as they can change.
travelTips.insuranceBody: Non-negotiable. It's your safety net for medical emergencies, trip cancellations, or lost baggage. Make sure your policy covers adventure activities like diving or hot air ballooning if they are on your itinerary.
travelTips.healthBody: No vaccines are mandatory for most itineraries, but proof of yellow-fever vaccination is required for travelers aged 9 months or older arriving from a country with yellow-fever transmission risk, including an airport transit there lasting more than 12 hours. Vaccine needs vary by person and route, so get destination-specific medical advice before travel. Outside large international hotels with confirmed treated water, use factory-sealed bottled or properly treated water for drinking, be mindful of food safety, and pack a small first-aid kit.
travelTips.budgetTitle: Crafting Your Budget: What to Expect in 2026 💰
travelTips.hack1: A delicious meal of Koshary or a Falafel sandwich can be an affordable option.
travelTips.hack2: The Cairo Metro is efficient and inexpensive for getting around the city.
travelTips.hack3: Many state-run sites offer reduced student tickets; commonly you must be 24 or younger and show valid student identification and an ISIC Card. Check each attraction.
travelTips.hack4: In local markets (souks), friendly bargaining is part of the culture.
travelTips.hack5: Purchase 1.5L bottles from supermarkets rather than small bottles from tourist stalls.
travelTips.stayLead: Finding the right place to rest your head in Egypt doesn't have to drain your wallet. From hostels to private guesthouses and hotels, you have several options.
travelTips.hostelsBody: Useful for meeting other travelers, but youth-style accommodation is not widely available, can be difficult to access, and shouldn't automatically be assumed to be 100% safe. Where available, expect around
travelTips.hotelsBody: For more privacy, budget hotels and private rooms cost around
travelTips.hotelsBody2: per night, depending on the city, location, facilities, and season.
travelTips.nubianBody: In Aswan, stay in a colorful, family-run Nubian guesthouse for a unique cultural experience. Prices vary considerably by property and services, so check current rates before booking.
travelTips.eatLead: Some of the most delicious meals you'll have in Egypt can still be affordable. The golden rule is to follow the locals and explore local food options.
travelTips.food1: The national dish. A hearty mix of rice, lentils, pasta, and spicy tomato sauce.
travelTips.food2: Made from fava beans, served in fresh pita bread.
travelTips.food3: Slow-cooked fava beans, the breakfast of champions.
travelTips.moveLead: Egypt is a large country, but its network of trains, buses, and local transport makes it easy to explore on a budget.
travelTips.trainsBody: A comfortable and classic way to travel long distances. Foreign-passenger pricing and booking access vary by train and class, and fares changed in March 2026. Check the official railway timetable and current fare for your date rather than relying on a fixed conversion.
travelTips.busesBody: Often the cheaper long-distance option. Check the operator's live timetable and fare for your date. Companies including Go Bus and Blue Bus serve long-distance routes, but route availability changes.
travelTips.microBody: For the truly adventurous. Inexpensive, but challenging to navigate without Arabic. Best for short, common routes where you can follow the locals' lead.
travelTips.wondersTitle: Experiencing Egypt's Wonders on a Budget 🏛️
travelTips.free1: Get lost in the sights and sounds of Khan el-Khalili in Cairo or the Aswan Old Souk. Window shopping is free!
travelTips.free2: Walk along the Nile promenade in Cairo, Luxor, or Aswan for beautiful sunset views.
travelTips.free3: Many of Cairo's older churches and mosques can be visited for free or for a small donation, depending on the site.
travelTips.free4: Take a low-cost public ferry to Elephantine Island. This is different from a private motorboat trip to a Nubian village; confirm the current public-ferry fare at the dock.
travelTips.itin1: See the Giza Plateau (700 EGP foreign-adult area entry, excluding pyramid interiors), the Egyptian Museum (550 EGP foreign adult), and Khan el-Khalili. Check the operator's live fare before booking an overnight bus or train to Luxor.
travelTips.itin2: Explore Karnak (600 EGP) and Luxor Temple (500 EGP) on the East Bank; Valley of the Kings (750 EGP, selected open tombs included) and Deir el-Bahari/Hatshepsut Temple (440 EGP) on the West Bank. These are foreign-adult prices checked in August 2026; premium tombs cost extra.
travelTips.itin3: Visit Philae Temple (550 EGP foreign-adult entry; boat transfer separate), explore a Nubian village, and take a sunset felucca ride. Abu Simbel site entry is 750 EGP for a foreign adult; transport or tour costs are additional.
travelTips.safeLead: A little preparation and respect go a long way in making your trip smooth and memorable.
travelTips.customsBody: Dress modestly, especially when visiting religious sites. A simple "Salam Alaikum" (hello) is always appreciated. Be respectful when taking photos of people.
travelTips.tippingBody: Tipping (baksheesh) is a part of life. Carry small notes (5, 10, 20 EGP) for porters at the airport, hotel staff, and bathroom attendants. A good tip for a full-day guide is around 300–500 EGP.
travelTips.safetyBody: Stay aware in crowded areas, avoid demonstrations, and use ride-hailing apps at night. For women's safety, dressing modestly and joining group tours can help minimize unwanted attention.
travelTips.ctaBody: Traveling to Egypt in 2026 on a budget is not only feasible but incredibly rewarding. With careful planning, an adventurous spirit, and a willingness to embrace the local culture, the timeless wonders of this ancient land are well within your reach.
travelTips.heroTagline: Your ultimate 2026 guide to budget travel in Egypt.
travelTips.schemaDescription: Practical Egypt travel tips from a Cairo-based licensed operator. Tipping, safety, scams to avoid, dress code, currency, transport, and what guidebooks usually get wrong.
travelTips.step2Body: Master your spending and find great deals.
travelTips.step3Body: Navigate like a local and see the best sights.
travelTips.headsUp: Don't assume every price tag is a steal. Inflation, currency shifts, and dual pricing (locals vs. tourists) can sometimes throw a curveball. A little vigilance goes a long way—think of it like bargaining in a souk: you don't need to haggle hard, just be informed and savvy with your spending.
travelTips.seasonABody: The perfect mix of decent weather, manageable crowds, and affordable prices. Airlines and hotels are often more generous with their deals. This is the best value for money.
travelTips.seasonBBody: If you don't mind serious heat, this could be your budget jackpot. Tailor your itinerary wisely with coastal time in Alexandria or Dahab. You'll find some of the lowest prices of the year.
travelTips.quickTip: Winter (Dec–Feb) has gorgeous weather but comes with a heavier price tag as it's peak tourist season. If your budget is tight, aim for the shoulder seasons.
travelTips.budgetLead: Let's talk numbers. A smart budget is your best travel companion. Exchange rates move frequently, so check a bank or reputable live currency source when you plan and again when you travel.
travelTips.figures: food, grocery, accommodation, tour, felucca, tipping and daily-budget amounts are local-market estimates, not fixed tariffs. They move with inflation and vary by city and season, so treat them as a planning guide and confirm current prices locally.
travelTips.dailyBudgetBody: Most budget travelers in Egypt should expect to spend somewhere between 2,500 and 3,000 EGP a day. Accommodation alone can run around 2,000 EGP per night, with the rest covering food, local transport, entrance fees, and other basic travel expenses.
travelTips.tripCost: Your total depends heavily on your accommodation, transportation, activities, and flights. Flights from the U.S. or Australia will generally increase the overall cost — your flight will likely be your biggest single expense.
travelTips.food4: Juicy, garlicky, and craveable chicken or beef wraps.
travelTips.selfCatering: Shopping at local markets is an adventure. A dozen eggs costs ~72 EGP, a loaf of bread is ~2.5 EGP, and fresh produce is incredibly cheap. This can be a useful way to save on breakfasts and lunches.
travelTips.localTransportBody: In Cairo, the Metro is a useful option for getting around the city. For taxis, use ride-hailing apps such as Uber, inDrive, or DiDi to get clearer pricing and avoid haggling.
travelTips.wondersLead: Entrance fees can add up, but with smart planning, you can experience Egypt's major attractions while managing your budget.
travelTips.itinLead: This classic “Golden Triangle” route combines Cairo, Luxor, and Aswan.
travelTips.itin4: Return to Cairo for departure or extend your trip to Alexandria or the Red Sea.

founder.heading: Hi, I'm Islam — and I built AffordEgypt to fix something I see every day.
founder.p1: I grew up in Aswan and have run a licensed Egyptian tour operator since {{year}}. We've taken thousands of travelers across Egypt: backpackers and families, honeymooners and solo first-timers.
founder.p2: Here's what I kept noticing: a huge number of travelers were getting priced out of real Egypt by tour operator markup and package bundling they didn't ask for. They'd either book a $4,000 package they couldn't afford, or take their chances with a fly-by-night WhatsApp operator nobody could verify.
founder.p3: AffordEgypt is the third option. The same licensed guides we send on our premium tours, the same vehicles, the same standards — stripped down to what you actually need. A private car. A real Egyptologist. And the freedom to add tickets, meals, and experiences only when you want them.
founder.closing: Real prices. Real operator behind it. Real Egypt.
